result.summary: Extracts handling logic for nine p2p message types out of the monolithic `PeerManagerImpl::ProcessMessage()` in `src/net_processing.cpp` into dedicated private helper functions. Each message handler is extracted in its own move-only commit with matching thread-safety annotations.
result.problem: `PeerManagerImpl::ProcessMessage()` is a roughly 1,000-line function handling numerous p2p message types inline, making navigation, scoping, and review in `net_processing` cumbersome.
evidence: PR description: '`PeerManagerImpl::ProcessMessage()` is a ~1000-line function handling every p2p message type inline, which makes it hard to navigate and review.'
PR description notes it continues the pattern established by merged commits fa5ab0220e (`ProcessPong()`) and fa55723b8f (`ProcessAddrs()`).
result.scope_notes: All changes are in `src/net_processing.cpp` and structured as move-only commits verifiable with `--color-moved`. The PR description lists seven extracted handlers, but the branch contains nine commits including `ProcessCompactBlock` and `ProcessVersion`.
result.card: Extracts handling logic for nine P2P message types out of `PeerManagerImpl::ProcessMessage()` in `src/net_processing.cpp` into dedicated helper functions. The function is an oversized monolith handling many message types inline, which makes navigating and reviewing `net_processing` difficult. The author notes this continues previously merged cleanup work splitting up the ~1,000-line function. This is a pure move-only refactoring across nine commits with no functional changes or dependencies.
